title: Arshdeep Singh Breaks Bhuvneshwar Record With 38 T20I Wickets in 2026
excerpt: The left-arm seamer's 2 for 33 against New Zealand in Christchurch took him past Bhuvneshwar Kumar's 37 wickets in 2022, in 26 innings, and level with Wanindu Hasaranga in the full-member list.
body:
• Arshdeep Singh took 2 for 33 in the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, taking his 2026 T20I tally to 38 wickets — a new India record for a calendar year.
  • He passed Bhuvneshwar Kumar's 37 wickets in 2022, reaching 38 in 26 innings compared with Bhuvneshwar's 31 innings.
  • Arshdeep dismissed Tim Seifert early and Glenn Phillips late; New Zealand recovered from 43 for three to finish 180 for five, with Phillips making 70 off 43 and Bevon Jacobs 58 off 46.
  • Among full-member nations, Ireland's Josh Little holds the overall calendar-year record with 39 wickets in 2022; Arshdeep is now level with Sri Lanka's Wanindu Hasaranga on 38.

India's left-arm fast bowler Arshdeep Singh became India's leading wicket-taker in men's T20 Internationals in a calendar year during the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday. Arshdeep returned figures of 2 for 33, taking his wicket tally in 2026 to 38 and surpassing Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who claimed 37 wickets in 31 innings in 2022, t2ONLINE reported.

The 27-year-old left-arm seamer reached the landmark in 26 innings. Cricketnmore, reporting IANS, confirmed the same figures: 2-33 in the second match, 38 wickets in 2026, and Bhuvneshwar's previous mark of 37 in 31 innings in 2022.

How the record fell in Christchurch

Arshdeep made an immediate impact, dismissing opener Tim Seifert early in the innings. His early breakthrough helped India restrict the hosts to 43 for three at the end of the powerplay, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Prince Yadav also contributing wickets, t2ONLINE reported. Cricketnmore gave the same powerplay score and the same wicket-takers.

New Zealand recovered after finding themselves at 41 for three in 5.2 overs. Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs produced a 116-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Phillips made 70 off 43 deliveries and Jacobs contributed 58 from 46 balls, helping New Zealand finish their 20 overs at 180 for five.

Arshdeep returned to remove Phillips with the final ball of the 18th over, according to Cricketnmore — the wicket that took him past Bhuvneshwar's record. t2ONLINE described the dismissal as particularly significant because it ended the partnership that had given New Zealand renewed hope after their difficult start.

Where Arshdeep stands in the full-member list

The achievement places Arshdeep among the most successful bowlers from full-member nations in men's T20Is in a single calendar year. Ireland's Josh Little holds the overall record with 39 wickets in 2022, while Sri Lanka's Wanindu Hasaranga claimed 38 wickets in 2024. Arshdeep is now level with Hasaranga and could move to the top of the list if he claims two more wickets before the end of the year, t2ONLINE reported.

Cricketnmore published the same full-member list: 39 by Josh Little in 2022, 38 by Wanindu Hasaranga in 2024, 38 by Arshdeep Singh in 2026, and 37 by Bhuvneshwar Kumar in 2022. It described Arshdeep as having the third-most wickets by a player from a full-member nation in a single year, behind Little and Hasaranga. PTI reporting cited in other coverage added that Little's scalps came largely against Associate Nations, and that Arshdeep had also taken 33 wickets in 2022 and 36 in 2024.

India's own calendar-year list underlines that consistency. Behind Arshdeep's 38 in 2026 and Bhuvneshwar's 37 in 2022 sit Arshdeep's 36 in 2024 and Varun Chakravarthy's 36 in 2025 in the lists published by Cricketnmore's syndicated coverage. Arshdeep appears three times in India's top five calendar years, a pattern no other Indian bowler in the list matches.

What the record says about his role

Both reports point to the same bowling profile: wickets in the powerplay and breakthroughs later in the innings. In Christchurch that meant Seifert in the opening phase and Phillips in the 18th over, at opposite ends of the innings, in the same match in which he set the record.

With the calendar year still underway and matches remaining in the series, Arshdeep has a direct route to the outright full-member record: two more wickets would take him past Little's 39. For Indian fans following the New Zealand tour from the diaspora, the next matches in the series now carry a second scoreboard — India's result, and whether their left-arm seamer finishes 2026 alone at the top of the calendar-year list.
